# 1 Maccabees Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_005_page_001.jpg

---

1. And it came to pass, when the nations round about heard that the altar had been rebuilt and the sanctuary rededicated as before, they were exceedingly angry.
2. And they took counsel to destroy the race of Jacob that was among them, and they began to slay and destroy among the people.
3. And Judas made war against the sons of Esau in Idumea, at Akrabattene, because they were besieging Israel; and he struck them with a great slaughter, and humbled them and took their spoils.
4. And he remembered the wickedness of the sons of Baean, who had been a trap and a stumbling block to the people, lying in wait for them on the roads.
5. And they were besieged by him in towers, and he encamped against them and utterly devoted them to destruction, and burned their towers with fire and all who were in them.
6. Then he crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and he found a mighty force and much people with Timothy as their head.
7. And he fought many battles with them, and they were defeated before him, and he struck them.
8. And he seized Jazer and her villages, and he turned back to Judea.
9. And the nations in Gilead gathered against the Israelites who were on their borders to destroy them; and they fled to the stronghold of Dathema,
10. and sent letters to Judas and his brothers, saying, "The nations around us have gathered against us to destroy us.
11. And they are preparing to come and capture the stronghold to which we have fled; and Timothy is the head of their force.
12. Now therefore come and rescue us from their hand, for many of us have fallen.
13. And all our brothers who were in the land of Tobias have been put to death, and they have led captive their wives and their children and their substance, and have destroyed about a thousand souls there."
14. While they were still reading these letters, behold, other messengers came from Galilee with their garments torn, bringing a report of similar purport,
15. saying, "The men of Ptolemais and Tyre and Sidon have gathered against us, and all the Galilee of the Foreigners is full of them, to destroy us."
16. And when Judas and the people heard these words, a great congregation was gathered to take counsel what they should do for their brothers who were in distress and being attacked by them.
17. And Judas said to his brother Simon, "Choose you men and go and deliver your brothers in Galilee; and I and Jonathan my brother will go to Gilead."
18. And he left Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azariah as commanders of the people, with the rest of the forces in Judea for the guarding of it.
19. And he commanded them, saying, "Take charge of this people, but do not engage in battle with the nations until we return."
20. And to Simon were given three thousand men to go to Galilee, and to Judas eight thousand men to go to Gilead.
21. And Simon went to Galilee and fought many battles with the nations, and the nations were defeated before him.
22. And he pursued them to the gate of Ptolemais; and there fell of the nations about three thousand men, and he took their spoils.
23. And he took the Jews who were in Galilee and in Arbatta, with their wives and their children and all that they had, and brought them to Judea with great joy.
24. And Judas Maccabeus and his brother Jonathan crossed over the Jordan and went three days' journey in the wilderness.
25. And the Nabateans met him and received him peaceably, and told him all the things that had happened to their brothers in Gilead.
26. and that many of them had been shut up in Bosora and Bosor in Alema and in Caspho, Maked, and Carnaim — all these cities were strong and great;
27. and that they were shut up also in the other cities of Gilead, and that on the morrow they were going to encamp against the strongholds and to take and destroy all these men in one day.
28. And Judas and his army turned suddenly and struck Bosora in the way, and took the city and slew all the males by the edge of the sword, and took all their spoils and burned the city with fire.
29. And they departed from there by night, and traveled until they came to the stronghold.
30. And at dawn, when they lifted up their eyes, behold, a great multitude, beyond numbering, carrying ladders and engines of war, to take the stronghold; and they were fighting against the garrison.
31. And Judas saw that the battle had begun and that the cry of the city went up to heaven with trumpets and a great clamor.
32. And he said to the men of his army, "Fight today for your brothers."
33. And he came with three companies in the rear of them, and they sounded the trumpets and cried in prayer.
34. And the army of Timothy realized that it was Maccabeus, and they fled before him; and he struck them with a great blow; and there fell of them on that day about eight thousand men.
35. And he turned aside to Maspha and made war against it; and he took it and slew all the males and took its spoils and burned it with fire.
36. From there he departed and took Caspho and Maked and Bosor and the other cities of Gilead.
37. Now after these things Timothy gathered another army and encamped before Raphon, beyond the stream.
38. And Judas sent men to spy out the army; and they brought back word to him, saying, "All the nations round about us are gathered to him, a very great force.
39. And they have also hired Arabians, and they have encamped beyond the stream, ready to come against you to battle." And Judas went to meet them.
40. And Timothy said to the commanders of his force, "When Judas and his army come near the stream, if he crosses over first to us, we will not be able to stand against him; for he will certainly prevail over us.
41. But if he is afraid and encamps beyond the stream, we will cross over to him and prevail against him."
42. And when Judas came near the stream, he stationed the scribes of the people near the stream and commanded them, saying, "Do not allow anyone to encamp; all must go over to the battle."
43. And he himself crossed over first against them, and all the people after him; and all the nations were defeated before him, and they cast away their weapons, and fled to the temple precinct in Carnaim.
44. And they took the city and burned the temple precinct with fire, with all who were in it; and Carnaim was subdued and could not stand before Judas.
45. And Judas gathered all Israel who were in Gilead, from small to great, with their wives and their children and their substance, an exceedingly great army, to come to the land of Judah.
46. And they came as far as Ephron; now this was a great city in the way, very strongly fortified, and there was no way to turn from it on the right hand or on the left, but they must go through the midst of it.
47. And the men of the city shut them out and blocked the gates with stones.
48. And Judas sent to them with words of peace, saying, "Let us pass through your land to go to our own land, and no one shall do you harm; we will only pass through on foot." And they would not open to him.
49. And Judas commanded proclamation to be made throughout the camp that each should set up camp where he was.
50. And the men of the army encamped there, and he fought against the city all that day and all that night; and the city was delivered into his hands.
51. And he slew all the males by the edge of the sword, and razed the city to the foundations and took its spoils, and passed through the city over the slain.
52. And they crossed the Jordan in the great plain over against Beth-shan.
53. And Judas was gathering the stragglers and encouraging the people all the way, until he came to the land of Judah.
54. And they went up to Mount Zion with joy and gladness and offered burnt offerings, because not one of them had fallen until they had returned safely.
55. In the days when Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Gilead, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais,
56. Joseph son of Zacharias, and Azariah, commanders of the forces, heard of their good deeds and of the battles they had fought.
57. And they said, "Let us also make a name for ourselves, and let us go fight against the nations who are around us."
58. And they gave orders to the men of their force, and went to Jamnia.
59. And Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
60. And Joseph and Azariah were routed, and were pursued to the borders of Judea; and there fell of the people of Israel that day about two thousand men.
61. And there was a great rout among the people, because they had not listened to Judas and his brothers, thinking to do bravely.
62. But they were not of the seed of the men through whose hands salvation had been given to Israel.
63. And the man Judas and his brothers were greatly honored in all Israel and before all the nations, wherever their name was heard.
64. And men gathered to them and blessed them.
65. And Judas went down with his brothers and fought against the sons of Esau in the land in the south; and he struck Hebron and her villages, and tore down her strongholds and burned her towers round about.
66. And he decamped to go into the land of the Philistines, and he passed through Marissa.
67. And there fell of the priests in the battle, desiring to do bravely, going out to fight without counsel.
68. And Judas turned aside to Azotus in the land of the Philistines, and he tore down their altars and burned the carved images of their gods with fire, and he plundered the spoils of the cities, and returned to the land of Judah.
